study_identification_part.si4_title: Normative Modeling of Thalamic Nuclear Volumes and Characterization of Lateralized Volume Alterations in Alzheimer's Disease Versus Schizophrenia

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The abstract clearly states the aim to establish novel normative models of thalamic nuclear volumes and laterality indices and to investigate their changes in schizophrenia and Alzheimer's disease. The main text further hypothesizes that normative modeling would identify shared and distinct changes between disorders, explicitly describing the purpose of applying normative modeling.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: "The aim of this work was to establish novel normative models of thalamic nuclear volumes and their laterality indices and investigate their changes in SCZ and AD."; "Therefore, we hypothesized that normative modeling of thalamic nuclear volumes would facilitate the identification of shared and distinct changes in thalamic nuclear regions between the 2 disorders."

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: Eligibility and data quality procedures are described. Controls were defined per cohort with typical development/aging and exclusion of major psychiatric/neurologic disorders in HCP cohorts, with original sources cited in the supplement. Image quality control included visual inspection of all segmentations with reprocessing or exclusion for failures, and outlier handling at the site level. Final sample sizes after QC are reported with counts by cohort.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "All segmentations were visually inspected... Participants with missing or failed segmentations were reprocessed or excluded."; "A total of 2954 of 2978 participants ages 5.6 to 100 years passed initial quality control procedures (Table 2 and Figure 1)."; "Unprocessed T1-weighted images and clinical measures were accessed from 7 cohorts (HCP DEV, HCP EP, HCP YA, UCLA, SCZ AH, HCP AGE, and ADNI) described in Supplemental Methods."; "All subjects (n=628...) were defined as controls and considered to have a broadly typical development that excluded a history of a serious medical or psychiatric condition" (HCP DEV); "All subjects... considered to be broadly healthy without a history of neurodevelopmental, psychiatric, or neurological disorders" (HCP YA); "...typical aging without major psychiatric or neurologic disorders" (HCP AGE).

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: Preprocessing steps are described, including eTIV adjustment via residual method, site harmonization using ComBat (NeuroHarmonize), mean centering, sex stratification for univariate models, and omission of these steps for multivariate models where covariates are included. Quality control procedures are described via visual inspection and exclusion/reprocessing of failed segmentations.
nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: "Volumes were first corrected for total intracranial volume (TIV); site effects were mitigated with ComBat in sex-stratified datasets as implemented in NeuroHarmonize Python library... volumes were then normalized by subtracting the mean (mean centering); and finally sex-stratified datasets were created."; "For TIV correction... eTIV was generated using the FreeSurfer mri_segstats binary."; "All segmentations were visually inspected... reprocessed or excluded."

nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.reason: A 5-fold cross-validation on control samples was used to evaluate models and select the top-performing approach prior to training on all controls, satisfying the internal validation criterion.
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: "A 5-fold crossvalidation was used to evaluate each model... The model with the best overall performance based on average mean absolute error (MAE) was selected and trained on all control samples for each region."
